primary_source.what_it_is_our_words: A company research article, published 2003-04-16, last modified 2016-03-25 (page meta). It reports a study — 44 users, 620 tasks, more than 8,000 clicks — and finds no correlation between click count and task success or satisfaction. The page's only rights statement is an all-rights-reserved footer.
primary_source.finding_receipt_le_15_words: Hardly anybody gave up after three clicks

permits_us: names-only — the study's FACTS in Apollo's words (44 users, 620 tasks, >8,000 clicks, no correlation between clicks and success or satisfaction) with a pointer to the article; the article's sentences stay out of node text; the two charts are images and doubly out
why_our_words: An inoculation node needs the finding, not the prose: 'a 2003 UIE study of 620 tasks found no relationship between click count and success' is a fact with a pointer. That is the same footing as R1's own-words rows. The prose and the charts are Center Centre's.
cheap_route_to_lift: Center Centre's contact page (https://centercentre.com/contact) is linked from the footer. Price: one message.
unproven: Whether the 2003 study was ever written up outside this article (a report or paper with different terms) — not searched. Price: one search.

pitfalls.what: The article's memorable line ('Hardly anybody gave up after three clicks') is exactly what a generator will want to quote. ≤15 words with attribution is inside the house quotation rule; anything longer has no licence behind it.
URL rot: uie.com redirects today; a node pointing at articles.uie.com depends on a redirect Center Centre may drop. Point at the canonical.
The two charts carry the evidence visually; a screen brief that reproduces a chart image copies an unlicensed asset.
